To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
S100P and pVHL are useful immunohistochemistry markers to distinguish primary ICCs from metastatic PDAs.
S100P is a highly specific marker for pancreatic ductal adenoma (PDA), pVHL is a specific marker for intrahepatic Cholangiocarcinomas (ICCs), and MUC5AC and CK17 are highly sensitive markers for PDA.
S100P/pVHL/MUC5AC/CK17 immunostaining may aid in distinguishing primary intrahepacthic cholangiocarcinarcoma from metastatic pancreatic ductadenocarcinoma.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the immunohistochemical distinction of intrahepatic primary cholangiocarcinaroma (ICC) from metastatic pancreatic ductadenocarcinoma on liver biopsy.

the immunohistochemical expression of S100 protein, von Hippel-Lindau tumor suppressor gene product, IMP3, MUC5A, maspin and cytokeratine 17 in pancreatic ductal adenoca and intrahepatic biliary adenoca.
the development of an immunohistochemical method that will allow pathologists to make a more confident distinction between primary ICC and metastatic PDA.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ICC and PDA can be reliably distinguished on liver biopsy by using a panel of four immunomarkers (S100P, p-VHL, MUC-5AC, and cytokeratin 17).
ICC and PDA are not always easily distinguishable on the basis of immunohistochemistry.
ICCs express pVHL and IMP3, and PDAs express MUC5AC and S100P.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
S100P+/MUC5+/CK17+/pVHL- staining pattern is indicative of PDA, whereas S100P-/MUC5-/CK17-/pVHL+ staining pattern is indicative for ICC.
pVHL is highly sensitive and specific for distinguishing between ICC and metastatic PDAs.
S100P+/MUC5-/pVHL-/CK17- immunoreactivity is indicative of ICC, S100P+/CK17+ immunoreactivity is suggestive of PDA, and S100P-/MUC5+/pVHL+/CK17- immunostaining is essentially diagnostic of PDA.
The main takeaway from our work is that
S100P is highly expressed in PDA and rarely expressed in ICC, whereas pVHL is highly expressed in ICC and rarely expressed in PDA.
S100P and pVHL are useful markers to distinguish between ICC and metastatic PDA on liver biopsy.
pVHL expression is seen in 71% of primary ICCs, whereas it is seen in only 5% of metastatic PDAs to the liver.
